newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower amid retreating packer demand following a steep decline in pork product prices on Wednesday, livestock dealers said.
Hog marketings also were slowing down as farmers resist the lower cash prices, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 lower at $57.00-$58.00 in the country and $58.00-$59.00 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 lower at $57.50 to $59.00 in the country and $59.50 at plants in light volume. Prices could sink further as the day progresses, Illinois dealers said.
"No one gives a hoot this morning, the packer doesn't want to pay these prices and the farmer doesn't want to sell," one central Illinois hog dealer said.
Indiana hogs sold $1.00 lower at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $59.00 at plants in thin trading, dealers said.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 lower at $55.50 to $56.50 in the country and $58.00 at plants.
Lower pork product prices plunged packer operating margins deeper into the red, the dealers said.
Pork cut-out values Wednesday were quoted down $2.58 to $2.71 per cwt, USDA reported.
